只能值个中等评价，6/10。 优点：rogue基础保障了一定的游戏性，叠加俄罗斯方块游戏模式，放大了游戏的可玩性。 缺点：下落机制的不完善，导致有一定的精力要浪费在左右左右或者切换保留方块，以延长下落时间这种毫无意义的操作上。说真的，不如直接改为发3-4张牌，然后按照俄罗斯方块下落的规则（包括旋转塞进角落的规则）直接拼块，这样还极大的简化了操作，让玩家的精力可以集中在阅读文字和计算收益这种核心事情上。这个缺点直接导致在游玩过程中的割裂感。
太随机了，卡牌也不够强力，开了水域直接崩盘。没有构筑卡牌的快乐，只有对随机方块的无奈。很多卡牌不够分明，目前就普通难度，一直卡关。 优点是玩法新颖

I want to be really clear, I do love what this game is presenting as its loop. However, I find the loop after several hours to be extremely shallow. You are met with sheer cliffs of difficulty spikes between Acts, for which there is zero means for you to effectively "outsmart" your way into a win. It's planned failure to force you to return to the main menu so you can start again with a/several boosted cards at your fingertips that you unlocked naturally without even thinking about it simply for the fact that you were following what the facility says you should already be doing to maximize its effectiveness. I would hazard to say that if you weren't trying to do that every time regardless, you'd just be jeopardizing your entire run due to the RNG potential of just being served a dearth of pieces that simply won't mesh with what you need to build to win the fight on that map, and all for a silly bonus when you inevitably have to restart. I enjoy Tetris a lot. I tend to feel clever when I manage to make the lines, and the strategy behind laying things in the order you need to max them out in this game is fun. But I *hate* that I'm told to go back and do it all again just because you want to force me to pad my time out content-wise by creating artificially scaled walls. I will continue to play this game, but honestly it's largely because it allows me to do so between calls from work easily. Without changes, it's just not respectful of time though, so I don't think it's worth it if you're coming into this expecting to be able to outsmart the rogueliteification. You won't. It's just a more fancy Tetris with a mini-game at the end. So yes, I do recommend this game... but at the same time, I don't.

创意优秀，但实际感受非常奇怪，我很难给出一个好评。 断断续续通关了普通模式，可以感受到游戏的内容非常丰富，但我目前解锁并体验到的部分可能都不到1/4。 游玩的过程里，我无法理解开发者对于这款游戏的侧重点，或者说开发者没有把俄罗斯方块、卡牌构筑、战斗这三个方面做出非常好的结合。 首先是战斗部分，非常简单的比大小，但经过一整局的精密运营或者是思考后，这种简陋的战斗或者说结算方式让我有种虎头蛇尾的感觉，非常平淡。如果说战斗并不是游戏强调的部分或者玩法，那么大可以省略掉，没有必要设置兵种，无非就是替换成分数作为过关的限制。 然后是俄罗斯方块与卡牌结合的玩法，创意好评，但是实际上手的体验并不好，方块的出现过于随机，玩家缺乏干扰基础方块出现顺序的手段，并且由于地形的限制，这让大部分游玩时间的方块放置并不能让玩家百分之百的满意，我认可这种难度机制的设计，但是面对这种负反馈无能为力的感觉非常影响游戏乐趣。 最后就要说到游戏乐趣的部分，游戏给我的感受非常微妙，打开游戏前感觉有点意思，但是游玩几回合后就觉得无聊，然后关掉。基于目前的游戏来看，开发者很难再去对基础框架做出大的改动，或许可以靠引入新的机制来改善。

A great idea that is reasonably executed, ruined by its meta progression system in the following ways: 1) Rather than a generalized "experience" meter that increases after every run based on the success of the run, the game opts for a quest-based system. This encourages you to hunt for specific cards and exploit them to complete quests (at the expense of your runs), and provides absolutely no direct benefit for actually winning (outside of the first time, which completes a quest). Whether you die in Act 1 or on the final boss in Act 3, you do not gain any direct meta progression benefit unless you are completing quests. 2) The unlockable tree is huge but basically linear. No meaningful choices to be made, except for whether or not you want to interact with the system at all. Because: 3) Unlocking gameplay elements makes the game worse, not better. This is the central problem with the system. Given the sheer volume of things you unlock, the size of the item pool bloats extremely fast. Unlike Slay the Spire, where you will have multiple dozen opportunities to add cards to your deck during a run you're only going to get 4 or 5 chances per act in Drop Duchy. So unlocking things dramatically decreases your ability to get impactful or synergistic cards, meaning that the game is punishing you for interacting with the meta progression system. And the more that you interact with it, the more cards you unlock, so the more the game punishes you. Even before you're 10 hours in, the item pool becomes so large, and the opportunities to select cards so limited, that it all just feels like a slot machine. Meanwhile, what does a successful run even get me? Either nothing (because I didn't play the way the quests wanted me to play), or an even more bloated item pool. I had a great time for the first few hours, but I'm already at the, "Why am I playing this, again?" stage, and probably won't return to the game.

Warning, this is long winded, I have a lot of thoughts. But tl;dr: Can't recommend. Feels like they came up with a cool, eye-catching idea of "City Builder Tetris Roguelike" and then struggled to come up with ways to expand upon it in interesting directions. If you care to know why, allow me to explain: - Most keywords don't explain what they do. - Tons of achievements are just padding, "Get thing X times", ect, so you can earn unlocks. - Said unlocks are uninteresting. Some are cool, but many are just a single card, or feel like they were hacked out of the base game to become unlockables and pad playtime. - Navigation is pointless. At forks, your options all offer the same 'type' of encounter. Some options also just suck way more than others, so you aren't even making a choice there. - Enemy encounters use the same cards as the players. It means every normal fight plays out the same. - You always fight the same boss each act. This means some cards and strategies that get countered by a boss will always be bad. - YOUR TETRIS PIECES ARE INCONSISTENT. This means you can set up a 4-line "clear" only to have all your line pieces buried at the bottom of the "deck" of pieces. If they're even there at all. The level of randomness was also a real sticking point for my experience. I know the game is trying to make me not play "normal tetris" and encourage me to make tough decisions that interact with its mechanics... but... 1) that feels awful, because you're only punished. 2) they put in a "Reload Save" button in the menu that lets you RESTART ANY ENCOUNTER. Let me ask you this: If you can easily replay any fight that doesn't go well due to bad RNG... then what's the point of even having the randomness at all? To waste my time until I get a good run-out? To top it all off, the higher difficulties are just horrifically challenging. and the RNG of getting randomly hard-countered or bad piece order only makes it more annoying. And perhaps that would be fine, people like hard challenges after all. But right near the end of the unlock tree you get the third playable faction, "The Order", which revolve around not one, but TWO "Super-Resources" in Faith and Crusaders, which SOLVE EVERY PROBLEM. (Other factions can unlock Faith, but they can't access it nearly as freely as The Order. Crusaders are Order faction unique though.) The Order feels so overtuned that it feels like a lot of the high-tier difficulty is balanced around it. But a Faith & Crusaders build is so powerful that it's the only build to go for. Anything that isn't that can't really compete, which overall results in a late-game where you're going for the exact same choices and build every time while fighting an uphill battle of annoying RNG. In summary: An interesting concept held back by a ton of unfortunate design decisions. Maybe there's a fun game in there somewhere, because the first two hours are actually pretty nice, but beyond that my experience grew more and more aggravating every time I played.

第一眼看是俄罗斯方块，实际上并没有太多的联系，主打的并非是整行消除，而是土地规划。 玩法方面还是很有趣的，最初的几个小时还在探寻整行填满的收益，直到发现适当的空格从而让整篇区域链接在一起的玩法才会让收益最大化，豁然开朗 但游戏有几个非常致命的缺点： 一、切牌槽只有一个，导致出牌顺序极为关键，这个问题在高难度下十分严重。前期三地块混出，很容易将你一局的规划全盘打乱，尽管可以通过左侧进场栏提前规划堆叠方向，但仍可能烂牌连出导致这局不得不SL。（尤其是手上两个都很恶心但偏偏第三块就是挽救局面的关键卡，这种感觉就像你黄片和手纸都准备好了，但下一张牌是老妈进屋找东西，再下一张牌是老爸进屋找你唠嗑） 二、科技树解锁十分不合理。游戏的局外成长是靠局内任务解锁的，而科技树则是解锁卡牌的。而随着科技树的解锁，有很多意义不明收益极低的牌会加入卡池，导致一段时间内越解锁越弱。甚至在前期会增加一种新地形，让前期早早就进入三地形局面，场地的复杂程度直接上升一个等级。（这感觉就像随着年纪长大你从买黄碟的少年成长为会上PH的青年，但每一页里都有gay片，网站还不让你屏蔽） 三、这点属于上一点的延申，随着科技树解锁，后续还有新系统的加入，如果你科技点不够就不要贸然开启新系统，开的太少会因不成体系而完全用不了。（短剧只能看前6集） 四、卡牌升级并无规律可循，有的牌每级都扩大范围，有的牌第三级才扩大范围，而升级的时候又不能预览卡牌接下来每个等级效果，经常因此纠结半天要不要升某张牌。 你要问我为什么写出这么多缺点，但还是好评，我只能说，游戏真的很好玩

After 8 hrs playing and managing to beat act 3, my experience with this game is, to put it simply, annoyed. Why is it annoying? Its because it suffers from 3 things that I find it annoying. Its progression system, its randomness and its lack of game mechanics. The progression system: You start out with the Duchy and thats it.... If you want to play the other clans, i.e The Republic / The Order, you have to unlock crowns to unlock each progression tree + tech [b]BEFORE[/b] unlocking those clans and I only manage to unlock The Republic after beating Act 3 to get enough crowns. I also have 0 idea how to get crowns, i.e I have no idea whether its based on achievements or progression or beating acts and I am 8hrs in.... So by the time I unlock that, I am either still invested in the game or not so yea... Do note that it takes [i]quite a lot[/i] of crowns to open the other clans. The lack of game mechanics: I dont know how the DLC is but for the base game, your cards are just either military ( fight ) or resources ( upgrades ). The problem is that the resources are for upgrading cards OR unlocking slots and thats generally it. And here is the kicker.... 90% of the time, you want to take military because fighting the enemy means the boss is weaker. You can generally just not fight and take a path that is peaceful and farm resources but you can just beat their military and get resources anyway... ( ppl state that its a good idea to take at least 1 peaceful path ). The randomness: Ok... this game has too much randomness that from the 6th to the 10th hr of playing it, I was tilted. I like the tetris idea of how placing your tiles determine how the battle is [b]BUT[/b]it's too random. Whats the point of having a "reserve slot" when the tile you want will be at the very end. Here is a simple example: Game gave me Ranger Base ( gets you more military the more forest its connected to ). Placed it down. Guess what? The next 8 pieces be river, field, enemy, enemy, my other building, field, river, forest... Like wot? And you wont know whats the next cards after that be. It might be forest, it might be others so you have a high chance not to even connect other forest tiles together. [Edit: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3722856124 example. I cant connect because I got training ground and mountain early. Those block the forest and I cant reserve because I need to get rid of the enemy horse stable. All that and I got the last 8 pieces as forest...] To add on, when you get your card rewards, its random too. Say you want more forest military cards. It can be production forest building, a river military or a forest building that makes it into a field. Like wot? Yes, you can reroll and yes you can banish the cards but still, its a roll of dice. Also the military card rewards dont feel like they do anything. There is no status (catapault-like to cause fire damage every turn or poison), no ailments (every turn, -5 strength or something). It just rock paper scissors. So what you got is a card deck game that have random tile drops that may determine your placement and military power as well as the enemies + random card rewards that may or may not be beneficial to you + a progression system that is, imo grindy and finally a lack of determination for me to learn the game because of the other 3 reasons ( I have 0 idea what overflow for river even means ). Its not a bad game, in fact, its a solid roguelite. It just has [b]way too much RNG[/b] and a slow progression system. In fact, all the acts should have been longer to slowly build your army vs oh lets fight all the fights to make the endboss weaker. [edit: just making this part clear. what I mean longer is in terms of like StS or dead cells where the maps or dungeons or combat areas are longer so that you can build your deck to be nicer and stronger and eventually topple the boss, not 3-4 fights + 2-3 pick what resources then boss fight. It doesnt feel like Im working towards something, more like " I hope I get the cards needed to win the fight "

玩那个b塔2两百个点后玩点这个真是沁人心脾啊 核心是通过合理的顺序和位置把区域之间的交互收益最大化 其实更像是下落版文明6 总体来说虽然运气成分很大 但至少遇到挫折的时候你很难说俄罗斯方块是坏的玩法 遇到的问题 1.教程的UI 地图的UI 和界面之间的切换做的很不舒服 （教程需要一个个点而没有列表、关卡内和选卡时都无法浏览整个地图、地图点击和滚动都有卡顿） 2.部落这个机制不太适配俄罗斯方块的玩法的 在一个随机下落同时要考虑摆放位置顺序的玩法里 把四个方块摆放成矩形并且把2*2的方块放在中间 完成这种操作风险和成本都极大 收益和风险不匹配 3.翻译和教学真的是太差了 和塔2那样直接把一些关键词做成提示挂在牌旁边比起来 很多实际游玩里建筑机制的关键词教程里都找不到 相关翻译又非常拗口 比如 “采集者小屋：与这个建筑相连的片区内，每有1个森林方格不在片区的边缘，就获得4金币生产” 包括河流的实际效果和卡组的介绍都不太匹配 十个小时我也没太明白河流应该怎么连接 直接画出来告诉大伙这个怎么用会好很多 4.前十个小时的体验内 构筑之间的涌现很少 同时卡组升级和解锁卡槽都对资源的要求极高 构筑的目的其实更多是维持资源平衡 这使得构筑本身不构成某种流派的玩法 只是在维持流派的玩法同时救火 虽然看过那种十字军数值后期数值爆炸的视频 但现在还没太遇到

Drop Duchy continues the modern trend of mashing together two random genres and seeing what happens. Unfortunately it doesn't really work here because the devs took shallow Roguelike Deckbuilder mechanics and combined it with off-brand Tetris. This could've worked if they followed the rules of the original Tetris 1:1, using the original pieces and original board size, but for some reason indie devs seem to want to reinvent the wheel every time. This game is fine for a weekend afternoon but becomes really unfun once you dig deeper into higher difficulties or Trials. The base game includes three factions: Duchy is the "vanilla" faction, The Republic is focused on building neighborhoods to buff their keystone, and The Order has two new resources to manage for bonuses. Even though you can disable card unlocks in the progress tree, each faction wants different archetypes and keywords, forcing you to filter out the chaff for your faction of choice in order to have a chance at progressing beyond normal difficulty. Duchy feels like training wheels and is too repetitive after a few unlocks. The Republic grows in strength with a weak early game and strong late game. The Order suffers the most from RNG though because of their keystone building's mechanics... I wish there were more basic factions that focused on terrain types or keywords, instead of sprinkling those design ideas throughout the unlocked cards. Drop Duchy seems intent on screwing you out of Tetrises unless you find a passive card that converts other blocks into line pieces. There's too many mechanics going on here for the balance to ever be satisfactory: card reward RNG, piece order and piece terrain type RNG, enemy pieces and their interactions with your pieces, the list goes on. Savescumming seems possible to a point, but there were many bad scenarios that were just absolute game overs because I just didn't have enough combat units to deal with the enemies. End of combat rewards include all card types so you might not even get the option for a combat building until it's too late. Like most modern Rogue-lites, victory is controlled more by RNG than skill. Drop Duchy would've worked better if it stuck to traditional Tetris rules (board size, piece shapes, line clears), and allowed more card filtering via archetype booster rewards. It's really awkward to grind achievements to unlock new content, only to then disable those new cards you unlocked. The gameplay was fine while getting my first win with each faction, but playing longer on Trials and attempting more achievement unlocks just frustrated me a lot. This is another average game that just falls on the "Not Recommended" side of the fence because of how frustrating it eventually becomes.

Drop Duchy is one of the first roguelites that attempts to introduce battling mechanics, and makes them utterly useless through the inclusion of their main game mechanic, Tetris. The only semblance of Strategy you can achieve when playing is by using cards that co-ordiante with what resource building you decide to use. Ex: If you use wood cleaners, you should use the troops that gain strength or number from plains/wheat fields. If you want forests, use Rangers etc. I say there is little to no strategy because you are effectively playing Tetris first, and Drop Duchy second. If you are not good at Tetris , you will not be good at this game. That is not a complaint. The complaint comes from the fact that you cannot do ANYTHING if you just draw bad pieces. Yeah, you can swap the shape with F once, but that wil rarely ever save you or let you actually build up any army. The Wall is a bad actor in this sense because the whole premise is that The Wall is as long as the Tetris Board, and will block you off from building more of an army/going up the top half of the board. You can DELAY the Wall Piece from coming into rotation by filling out layers. You will rarely ever get to fill out layers because you'll rarely ever draw needed pieces, nor have any counter-play to get good pieces if you draw duds. Progression is not very good either. instead of each level adding something unique that makes further progression more fun or at the very least easier, Drop Duchy has none of that. You basically just constantly reload into games after Dying before beating Act 1 because you just outright DO NOT HAVE ENOUGH TROOPS to beat certain Act 1 Bosses until you gain buildings that scale fast enough to equal the troops you fight on The Wall (usually between 65-130, you start with maybe 40 with optimal play.) This just makes you have to brute force games where you die early for fractions of EXP just to not even get a building you want. The upgrades you unlock don't progress linearly or line-up strategically, ex: one branch is specifically for archer troops or one upgrade branch specifically for melee troops. Drop Duchy just throws whatever the hell at the Tree. You don't stand a fair chance against anythiung, and the game intentionally pushes you towards that mindless loop of 5 minute games where you die early just so you can get enough XP to progress a single stage. Some Roguelite fans might enjoy this but I view it as poor game design if the player has no agency until he has dumped 5-6 hours into grinding nothing-burger games for morsels of EXP. Just general poor game design, as well as an art style that is weirdly inconsistent and contrasts itself negatively (the map terrain vs the actual tetris board is 3-D models vs pixel art) The Developers should have focused on making A Tetris roguelite based around Tetris mechanics, not try to shove some army battling mechancis into a game of Tetris. Because now those army battle mechanics end up being useless, and you only ever benefit by playing good tetris, not by choosing the right cards or strategizing who goes where (troop wise not piece wise). I don't care enough to rant about the DLC, but any complaint about the base game can apply to the DLC's. "New Ways to fight!" MY ASS, when you just get given a new skin for the army knowing damn well the effects and stats of the buildings dont matter and you just need to play good tetris. You only ever win by playing good tetris, because that makes the Enemy Troop count drop drastically, which is the only chance you stand AT ALL against any boss in Acts 1-3. It feels very unfair and makes the skill tree and picking what towers I bring ultimately pointless when I just need to bring *some kind* of tower so I have troops, and then just play good tetris to make sure they dont have troops. The only thing that matters is playing Tetris, which I would have rather not payed $20 for and played online or in local arenas for free/a quarter. The army mechanics are ultimately useless, no matter how much I tried to reason out where they are actually required. The sole reason they exist is to give you a numerical value to compare to the enemies which you can only really ever effect by playing good tetris. Maybe I missed the point of the game, but if the point of the game is to just play tetris with the vague illusion of army building even mattering, it's just not my cup of tea

I picked this up from Humble Bundle and after 19 hours, I'm out. Great game on easy, solid game on normal, but I don't think it'll hold up for me on the higher difficulties. One thing this game has going for it is how forgiving it is. Unlimited single-turn undo, easy reload to attempt your last match over with some tweaks. This forgiveness without allowing full on scumming makes for engaging tactical runs without punishing fat-fingering or misunderstanding how a piece or card works. The UI is a little rough around the edges but the pieces work well together (ha). Actions are snappy, music is fine (I played this muted mostly but listened sometimes), and I was never surprised by something not working. Factions are well diversified and I completed a run with four out of five. Faction unlocks feel good but I didn't dive too wide into the trees. Trying to bend runs to hit goals and unlock more cards is fun, especially on the lower difficulties. I'm not a card game or a strategy guy, but I really enjoyed the synergy here, solid 8/10

～以俄罗斯方块为基础，将下落的方块替换为地形、建筑等模块。当一行被完全填满时，该行不会消失，而是会根据方块的具体构成，自动转换为相应的资源。 ～这些资源将用于强化携带的建筑。每局游戏的目标不再是堆叠更多方块，而是在有限方块摆放完毕，或方块堆积超出顶部线时，进行兵力比拼。玩家需要摆放的建筑，除己方的还有敌方的。每局结束时，系统将根据建筑特性计算产出的兵力，双方依据兵种的类型与数量进行消耗，以此决定本局的胜负走向。 ～每个可玩阵营都拥有独特体系的初始建筑。基本上，每局游戏都要依靠这些自带建筑和被动效果来构建阵容，一方面没有太多资源去升级其他建筑，另一方面后期卡池太杂，不容易抽到所需的建筑。此外，每场战斗中建筑的出场顺序也是随机的，不可能每次都拥有理想的位置。
